newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle sell brisk at $67- feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle sell brisk at $67- feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold at $67.00, down $1.00 compared with Wednesday, in active late sales amid steep declines in Chicago Mercantile Exchange live cattle futures, feedlot sources said.
Sales started light near midday but escalated once the futures market closed lower at 1300 CST, they said.
An estimated 35,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, which brought the week to date figure close to 105,000, the sources said.
This week's Panhandle showlist reportedly was cleaned up following Thursday's sales, they said.
About 9,000 head were sold in Kansas, bringing the week to date figure close to 76,500, feedlot sources said. The showlist in Kansas was close to sold out, but still had some cattle left, they said.
Showlists were estimated early in the week at 100,000 for the Panhandle and near 82,000 for Kansas.
Fed cattle price weakness was also tied to ideas that beef prices were starting to level off following moderate gains this week, they said.
Beef prices were quoted up $0.06 to $0.24 per cwt, with 174 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.
Heavyweight choice beef was up $0.06 at $103.59, up $1.80 since last Friday, when prices started recovering from steep declines the previous week, USDA statistics showed.
